title: Did Saudi Arabia Change Its Law for Ronaldo?
on_screen_hook: WHAT DID SAUDI DO FOR HIM?

story_spine.character: Cristiano Ronaldo, a forward of thirty-seven with no club when this starts, who cries in a dugout at thirty-nine and again at forty-one when he finally wins the league
story_spine.question: What did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
story_spine.driving_question: So what did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
story_spine.cold_open: 3 Jan 2023: he sits at the press table in Riyadh and says South Africa. It gains meaning at the last line, which returns to that table: this first ordinary, human moment is where every later claim about what the kingdom did for him began.
scenes: Nov 2022 to Jan 2023: Morgan, United exit, Morocco; Al-Muammar's account of who moved first; the fireworks at Mrsool Park; Amnesty the next day
Jan to Feb 2023: Georgina, no conversion, 'bent the laws'; first money reports; the Four Seasons; the debut
June 2023 to Feb 2024: the state fund, the record spend; the 99 lashes rumour; a real ban
May 2024: thirty-five goals, then King's Cup tears, four days apart
May to Dec 2025: 'this chapter is over', the extension and every pay figure; our maths; tourism, White House, villas, the beach story
Feb to May 2026: the reported protest, a fourth lost final, then the title at forty-one
The answer: back to the law question; then Aug to Oct 2026, forward through the wedding to the record's one idea
story_spine.thesis: The record shows reported money going one way and attention the other, and no law we could find rewritten for one man; why each side did it we can't prove.
story_spine.payoff: He did marry her, in Portugal; reported money went one way, attention the other, motives unproven, and we found no record of a law rewritten for him.
story_spine.loop_line: And we found no record of a law rewritten for the man who once sat at that press table.

beats.narration: Cristiano Ronaldo sat at a press table in Riyadh and told the world he'd come to South Africa.
beats.on_screen: Hook text: WHAT DID SAUDI DO FOR HIM?
beats.visual_intent: 15_south_africa_slip.mp4, segment 12.0-17.5: the slip itself on frame 1.

beats.narration: He meant Saudi Arabia. He'd just signed for Al-Nassr, on a contract that has never been *published*.
beats.on_screen: Label: 3 Jan 2023, Riyadh. Small line: REPORTED FIGURES ONLY, CONTRACT NEVER PUBLISHED. Optional text: South African Tourism replied it was 'patiently waiting' (SBS).

beats.narration: That silence filled up with pay figures, a rewritten law, and the closed beach story you may have heard.
beats.visual_intent: Fast teaser: 71_card_table_pay_by_season.png, 79_card_claim_law_changed.png, 80_card_claim_beach.png (top halves only, verdicts cropped so the answer stays withheld).

beats.narration: So what did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
Two months earlier he'd told Piers Morgan he felt betrayed by Manchester United. His contract ended, and after the World Cup he was thirty-seven with no club.
beats.on_screen: Label: Nov-Dec 2022. Ended by mutual agreement (AP).

beats.narration: So who approached first? The only first-hand account is from Al-Nassr's president then, Musalli Al-Muammar, three years later.
beats.on_screen: 77_card_timeline_joining.png. Line: AL-MUAMMAR'S ACCOUNT ONLY, VIA SUMMARIES.

beats.narration: He said a Saudi prince proposed it in July twenty twenty-two, and that contacts led to a meeting in Lisbon overseen by the sports minister.
beats.on_screen: Card 77, July 2022 row. Pull-quote: 'wanted reassurance that it was a big project' (relayed summaries). Mendes vs Regufe dispute off the voice; on screen if room. Family-member contact stays OFF voice and OFF card.

beats.narration: We found nothing from Ronaldo confirming that.
beats.on_screen: On screen: PIF 75%, 5 June 2023. No source gives PIF a role in the 2022 approach.

beats.narration: On December thirtieth Al-Nassr announced him, with no transfer fee reported. Four days later he came through the fireworks at a sold-out Mrsool Park.
beats.on_screen: Label: Mrsool Park, Riyadh. 25,000 capacity per The National.

beats.narration: The next day, Amnesty International said his signing fit a wider pattern of sportswashing.
beats.on_screen: Pull-quote: 'fits into a wider pattern of sportswashing', Amnesty, Dana Ahmed, 4 Jan 2023. Amnesty's characterisation; urged him to raise human rights. 81 executed in one day in 2022, per Amnesty.

beats.narration: And he hadn't come alone. Georgina Rodriguez came with him, both foreigners, unmarried, in a country where reports said living together outside marriage was forbidden.
beats.on_screen: On screen: reports cite no statute. 'Lived together unmarried until August 2026.'
beats.visual_intent: 12_arrival_georgina_flowers.jpg, 27_riyadh_skyline_dusk.jpg. Adults only in frame; no framing on the children.

beats.narration: He's not a Muslim convert, as far as any record shows, and we found no statement from him about his faith.
beats.on_screen: 82_card_claim_conversion.png: altered images, per fact-checkers. Sujood, May 2023: filmed, never explained by him; no sujood clip exists, so text only. Faith label stays off screen beyond 'no conversion, per fact-checkers'.

beats.narration: Headlines said special permission. One post quoted in Newsweek said he made them bend their laws instead of just marrying her.
beats.on_screen: Pull-quote: 'He made them bend their laws instead of just marrying her.' X user, via Newsweek, Jan 2023.
beats.visual_intent: Text over 28_riyadh_night_from_iss.jpg (second use) or 17_georgina_mrsool_pitch.jpg cropped so the children aren't featured.

beats.narration: Hold on to that one.
On the money, CBS reported about seventy-five million dollars a year basic.
beats.on_screen: 72_card_compare_original_deal_2022.png, top. Tag REPORTED.

beats.narration: Other reports put the full package near two hundred million euros a year, split never published.
beats.on_screen: Card 72 lower half, then 85_card_quote_no_world_cup_clause.png.

beats.narration: Home was a Four Seasons suite in Kingdom Tower, reported at up to three hundred thousand dollars a month.
beats.on_screen: 84_card_list_where_he_lives.png, top. No hotel price published.

beats.narration: One later report says a villa in Riyadh, but we couldn't confirm where he lives now.
beats.on_screen: Card 84 bottom line, district on the card only (Robb Report).
beats.visual_intent: 32_diplomatic_quarter_drive.mp4 seg 84-91 as generic Riyadh, never implied as his home.

beats.narration: By January tenth the club's Instagram was up more than a thousand percent.
beats.on_screen: 87_card_list_what_saudi_got.png, first row: about 11m. All platforms, under 5.2m to over 57.5m, Football Benchmark, March 2025.

beats.narration: He debuted as captain, and within three weeks scored all four in a four-nil.
beats.on_screen: Label: Debut, 22 Jan 2023. First goal 3 Feb, four v Al-Wehda 9 Feb on screen.

beats.narration: That June the state fund took control of his club. That summer Saudi clubs spent a record nine hundred fifty-seven million dollars, his part in it argued.
beats.on_screen: PIF 75%, 5 June 2023. Card 87, third row (Deloitte). Benzema, Neymar on screen. Causation argued, not proven. 12 Aug 2023: Arab Club Champions Cup, both goals in the final, ESPN calls it unofficial; his only final win there until May 2026.

beats.narration: One rumour had Iran sentencing him to ninety-nine lashes, until Iran's embassy in Spain denied any ruling.
beats.on_screen: 81_card_claim_99_lashes.png.

beats.narration: But Saudi rules did reach him. In February twenty twenty-four, a gesture at fans chanting Messi cost him a one-match ban.
beats.on_screen: On screen: SAR 10,000 fine, non-appealable, via Al Jazeera.
beats.visual_intent: 50_al_shabab_feb2024_match_official.mp4 (the gesture itself isn't in the listed segments).

beats.narration: He kept scoring, thirty-five league goals by May twenty-seventh, a Saudi record.
beats.on_screen: 78_card_timeline_football.png row. Guinness.

beats.narration: Four days later, the King's Cup final in Jeddah went to penalties. He scored his. Al-Nassr lost.
beats.on_screen: Label: King's Cup final, 31 May 2024.

beats.narration: He sat in the dugout in *tears* while staff tried to comfort him.
Forbes, which only estimates, put his football income at two hundred million dollars that season, then two hundred twenty-five million the next.
beats.on_screen: 71_card_table_pay_by_season.png rows, 76_card_chart_forbes_on_off_field.png. Forbes windows differ from seasons. 2024/25: third in the league.

beats.narration: In May twenty twenty-five he posted that this chapter was over.
beats.on_screen: "This chapter is over." 26 May 2025, after 3-2 at Al-Fateh.
beats.visual_intent: 37_chapter_over_apr2025.jpg (April photo; no date claim on it).

beats.narration: A month later he signed for two more years.
beats.on_screen: 26 JUNE 2025. Contract to June 2027.

beats.narration: The Sun, from unnamed sources, printed a hundred seventy-eight million pounds a year plus a signing bonus, one tabloid, unconfirmed, and the only breakdown for this season.
beats.on_screen: 73_card_list_extension_the_sun.png; card 71 row 2026/27. Card 71 line to add: NBC's $468m, unattributed, excluded.

beats.narration: Forbes estimated two hundred thirty-five million dollars for the year to May twenty twenty-six.
beats.on_screen: 74_card_breakdown_forbes_division.png top half: ESTIMATE.

beats.narration: Our own maths on that *estimate* gives about nineteen point six million a month, four and a half million a week, six hundred forty-four thousand dollars a day.
beats.on_screen: Card 74 rows, OUR DIVISION tag always visible.
beats.visual_intent: Card 74, row by row on the words.

beats.narration: A per-match fee? None has been reported. Divide by his thirty-seven games that season and it's about six point three five million dollars a game, our arithmetic, not his contract.
beats.on_screen: 75_card_table_per_match.png: NO APPEARANCE FEE HAS BEEN REPORTED. Stake: 83_card_claim_stake.png, reports only, on screen.

beats.narration: Saudi Arabia got his face on a tourism campaign. In November twenty twenty-five he sat at the White House dinner for its Crown Prince, and in Riyadh said he considered himself Saudi.
beats.on_screen: Source line: Visit Saudi, Sept 2025. Pull-quote: 'I consider myself Saudi', TOURISE, Nov 2025. No ambassador title found. Club denied a World Cup bid clause (card 85).

beats.narration: That December he and Georgina bought two villas on a Red Sea island.
beats.on_screen: Card 84 Nujuma row; price is The Sun's, screen only. Bought, not a gift, as far as reported. Reached by boat or seaplane.

beats.narration: The story you may have heard goes further, a whole Saudi beach closed for a day for his family.
beats.on_screen: 80_card_claim_beach.png claim line.

beats.narration: We searched in English and Arabic and found no report, couldn't trace it, and can't disprove it.
beats.on_screen: Card 80: UNVERIFIED; nearest is the unconfirmed Riyadh park closure.

beats.narration: In February twenty twenty-six, ESPN's sources said he sat out a match, protesting the state fund's lack of signings.
beats.on_screen: ESPN sources. No comment from Ronaldo found. League to BBC Sport: "no individual - however significant - determines decisions beyond their own club."
beats.visual_intent: Text panel with the league quote over 23_pif_tower_night.jpg.

beats.narration: That May he lost another final, at home, his fourth at Al-Nassr by ESPN's count.
beats.on_screen: 16 May 2026: 0-1 v Gamba Osaka, AFC Champions League Two.

beats.narration: Five days later he scored twice against Damac and won the league, at forty-one, in tears again.
beats.on_screen: Label: 21 May 2026, 4-1 v Damac. Tears per reports. First league title for the club since 2018/19.

beats.narration: So, did Saudi Arabia change its law for him?
beats.visual_intent: Near-still on 28_riyadh_night_from_iss.jpg; riser ends on the reveal cut.

beats.narration: The truth was, nobody has shown that it did. We found no *decree*, no regulation, no official statement either way. The story traces to two anonymous lawyers, who told the agency EFE the ban stood but authorities had stopped interfering with foreigners generally. That's a blind eye described for foreigners, not a law bent for one man.
beats.on_screen: 79_card_claim_law_changed.png: NO EVIDENCE (sound-off match). Sources: EFE via Bio Bio; Al Jazeera 2019. Hotel rule (2019, general, predates him) on card. Card 79 line to add: UK FCDO advice, 'Sex outside of marriage and adultery are illegal, including for tourists'; it does not address cohabitation. No statute named. Keep this line away from the couple's names.
beats.visual_intent: Card 79, row by row on the words.

beats.narration: And he did marry her, on August eleventh, twenty twenty-six, in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, not Saudi Arabia. He said in Vogue this is probably his last year. He's on about nine hundred eighty-five goals, suspended by Portugal's federation with no final ruling, his deal ends in June twenty twenty-seven, and RedBird has confirmed early interest in the club. Here's the record. Reported money went one way, attention the other. Why each side did it, we can't prove. And we found no record of a law rewritten for the man who once sat at that press table.
beats.on_screen: Name card during the line: CRISTIANO RONALDO. Small lines: pay figures are estimates; Portugal out to Spain, July 2026; Portuguese FA suspension, Oct 2026, no final ruling; 86_card_stat_goals_985.png; RedBird: preliminary, no deal announced.
beats.visual_intent: 58_wedding_bands_hands.jpg, 63_cascais_estoril_bay.jpg, card 86, 48_title_phone_angle_vertical.mp4, then 15_south_africa_slip.mp4 lead-in so the loop lands on b01.

publish.title: Did Saudi Arabia Change Its Law for Ronaldo?
publish.description: How Cristiano Ronaldo went from Manchester United to Riyadh, what was reported about his pay, and what we could and couldn't find on the claims about Saudi law and a closed beach. All pay here is estimated: his contract has never been published, and every per-month, per-day and per-game figure is our own division of a press estimate. A documentary on a living person, built from sourced reports.
publish.comment_prompt: If the contract were published tomorrow, which number do you think would turn out closest: Forbes or The Sun?
publish.pinned_comment: Sources: CBS, AFP via GOAL, Forbes via Wikipedia, The Sun via GOAL/SI, EFE via Bio Bio, Al Jazeera 2019, UK FCDO, Newsweek, Amnesty, ESPN, AP, UPI. Pay is estimated; contract unpublished; divisions are ours. We found no report of the beach story and couldn't trace or disprove it. Which is closest, Forbes or The Sun?
